subject: Sizing: Dedicated fleet consolidation & session morphology for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ian Foster <ian.foster@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-30T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing: quick clarifying questions before our tech call

Ian — thanks again for the time this morning. To make our engineering call tomorrow actionable, could you confirm a few things about the workloads you described? Short bullets are perfect.

1) Average prompt length (tokens) and typical response length (tokens) for each product surface (patient triage, clinician summarization, admin automation). If you track median and p95, include both.
2) Concurrency profile: typical concurrent sessions during business hours and peak concurrency windows (minutes/hour).
3) Session behavior: how often are sessions resumed (long-lived KV cache) vs one-off requests? Any callouts about multimodal payloads?
4) SLA target: p95 latency target for interactive flows and acceptable cold-start bounds.
5) Any constraints on model quantization or required model variants (FP16, int8)?

I've attached a one-page snapshot template and a small sample session CSV to fill; filling the CSV will let our pre-sales sizing tool generate an initial fleet sketch before we meet.

Looking forward — we want to show a few capacity tradeoffs (dedicated pool vs reserved burst) using your actual token distributions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurelia-sizing-snapshot.xlsx (xlsx), session-profile-sample.csv (csv)

From: Ian Foster <ian.foster@aureliahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: quick clarifying questions before our tech call

Marissa — really helpful list, thanks. Quick answers below. I copied ops@aureliahealth.com for any infra details they want to add.

1) Prompt/response: patient triage = prompt median ~60 tokens, response median ~180 tokens; clinician summarization = prompt median ~350 tokens, response median ~600 tokens (p95 ~1500); admin automation = small prompts ~20/30 tokens.

2) Concurrency: baseline concurrently active sessions ~120 (US business hours), typical peaks up to ~450 for isolated events (we see ~10–15 minute spike windows), sustained peak daypart ~90 mins during morning syncs.

3) Session behavior: clinician flows maintain long-lived sessions with KV reuse (~20% of sessions resume within 12h). Patient triage is mostly one-off. Multimodal: low-volume attachments (scanned docs) for clinician summarization, not heavy.

4) SLA: interactive flows we aim p95 < 600ms. Cold-starts acceptable up to 2.5s for background jobs, but for clinician-facing summaries prefer <1.5s.

5) Quantization: we prefer not to rely on aggressive quantization for clinician summaries — FP16 or int8 with validation is OK but need to validate quality delta on our prompts.

Happy to elaborate on the tech call.

—Ian
Ian Foster
CTO, Aurelia Health
ian.foster@aureliahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ian Foster <ian.foster@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: quick clarifying questions before our tech call

Thanks Ian — that level of detail is perfect. Ben / Karthik — looped you in on the prompt shapes.

Ben: based on the clinician summarization numbers (median 350 / response 600, p95 ~1500) and the concurrency spikes to 450, initial hypothesis is a hybrid approach: a dedicated pool sized for sustained baseline + an elastic reserved burst slab to cover 95th-percentile spikes without overcommitting GPUs.

Karthik: can you run a quick sketch with these inputs? I attached the filled CSV and our one-pager — if you can return a delta tradeoff between two config sets (conservative & aggressive) before tomorrow's call that would help the convo.

Ian: we'll also include a quick quality-sensitivity test plan (FP16 vs int8) so we can validate on a small holdout prompt set before committing.

Attaching: aurelia-sizing-snapshot.xlsx (filled), session-profile-sample.csv (filled)

—Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: quick clarifying questions before our tech call

Quick notes from a capacity angle after a first pass on the CSV:

• Baseline sustained concurrency of 120 with median token lengths maps to roughly 2x of a small A100-like instance group if we prioritize latency SLOs. For p95 latency under 600ms on clinician flows, we'll need to avoid packing those on oversubscribed instances.
• Spikes to 450 for 10–15 minutes indicate a need for fast scale-out (reserved burst or warm standby). Warm standby (pre-warmed hosts with scheduler ramp) reduces cold-start risk but has higher commit.
• Session-resume behavior (~20% long-lived) suggests a small tier of cached KV-friendly hosts to reduce repeated KV reconstruction costs. We can run a simulation to compute KV hit improvement for a 10% cache pool.

I'll attach a first-pass sketch (separate doc) during the call prep — Karthik if you can run the p95 simulation with two quant profiles (FP16 baseline, int8 conservative), we can include a quality gate threshold.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ian Foster <ian.foster@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: quick clarifying questions before our tech call

Ian / team — attached is a compact capacity sketch and two configuration options (conservative: higher dedicated V100-equivalent footprint; aggressive: smaller dedicated pool + 40% reserved burst). Key takeaways in the doc:

1) Conservative config meets p95 < 600ms for clinician flows without any int8 quantization, cost +35% vs aggressive.
2) Aggressive config uses an int8-validated model variant for background admin flows and FP16 for clinician summaries; shows ~20% lower monthly cost but requires a validation gate (10k holdout prompts).
3) We recommend a small KV cache tier sized at ~8–12% of instances to optimize session-resume flows; that reduces token compute by roughly 7–9% in our sim.

Next steps: schedule a 45-minute call to walk the sketch and run live QPS/p95 simulations with your sample prompts. I added two links in the doc: a HubSpot deal tracker and a Drive with the simulation notebook.

Cheers — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
